About Coronary Artery Disease 
 Another name for Coronary artery disease (CAD) is ischemic heart disease (IHD). It refers to a group of diseases which involves stable angina, unstable angina, sudden cardiac death and myocardial infarction. It is one of the cardiovascular diseases which is the most common type. A common symptom is discomfort or chest pain which may radiate towards the arm, shoulder, back, neck, or jaw. Occasionally it may feel like heartburn. Usually it occurs with exercise or emotional stress which lasts for less than a few minutes and which improves with rest. Shortness of breath may also occur and sometimes it is asymptomatic. The first sign of this disease is heart attack. Other complications are also there which includes heart failure and heartbeat which are abnormal.

Chest pain which occurs regularly after eating, with activity or at other time is called as stable angina and is associated with the constriction of the arteries of the heart. Angina that changes in character, intensity or frequency is called as unstable angina. Unstable angina may leads to myocardial infarction. About 30% of adults have pain due to coronary artery disease who go to the emergency department with an unclear reason of pain. 
 Dyspnoea, Weakness and numbness in any body part can also be seen in the case of coronary artery disease. 

 How to Diagnose Coronary Artery Disease? 
 For people which such symptoms, stress echocardiography can be used to diagnose obstructive coronary artery disease. The use of stress cardiac imaging, echocardiography, or advanced non-invasive imaging is not recommended in the individuals who are asymptomatic and are at decreased risk for developing coronary disease.

 About Coronary Artery Disease 
 Another name for Coronary artery disease (CAD) is ischemic heart disease (IHD). It refers to a group of diseases which involves stable angina, unstable angina, sudden cardiac death and myocardial infarction. It is one of the cardiovascular diseases which is the most common type. A common symptom is discomfort or chest pain which may radiate towards the arm, shoulder, back, neck, or jaw. Occasionally it may feel like heartburn. Usually it occurs with exercise or emotional stress which lasts for less than a few minutes and which improves with rest. Shortness of breath may also occur and sometimes it is asymptomatic. The first sign of this disease is heart attack. Other complications are also there which includes heart failure and heartbeat which are abnormal. 
 What are the Causes of Coronary Artery Disease? 
 This disease can affect people of any age and can occur at any point of life. This disease can be congenital and another reason can be the changed lifestyle and eating habits. The most common cause of the coronary artery disease is atherosclerosis. 
 What are the Risk Factors of Coronary Artery Disease? 
 
 Risk factors include high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, lack of exercise, high blood cholesterol, obesity, poor diet, depression, and excessive alcohol intake. 
 Age is also the risk factor because the risk of this disease increases with the growing age. 
 Males are at greater risk of developing coronary artery diseases rather than females. 
 An unbalanced diet which consists of high amount of carbohydrates and fats is also another risk factor for coronary artery disease. 
 
 What is the Pathogenesis of Coronary Artery Disease? 
 According to some studies, the underlying mechanism involves the reduction of oxygen and blood flow to the heart muscles and the reason behind this is again atherosclerosis. 
 What are the Signs and Symptoms of Coronary Artery Disease? 
 
 Chest pain which occurs regularly after eating, with activity or at other time is called as stable angina and is associated with the constriction of the arteries of the heart. Angina that changes in character, intensity or frequency is called as unstable angina. Unstable angina may leads to myocardial infarction. About 30% of adults have pain due to coronary artery disease who go to the emergency department with an unclear reason of pain. 
 Dyspnoea, Weakness and numbness in any body part can also be seen in the case of coronary artery disease. 
 
 How to Diagnose Coronary Artery Disease? 
 For people which such symptoms, stress echocardiography can be used to diagnose obstructive coronary artery disease. The use of stress cardiac imaging, echocardiography, or advanced non-invasive imaging is not recommended in the individuals who are asymptomatic and are at decreased risk for developing coronary disease. 
 The following tests helps in proper diagnosis of coronary artery disease: 
 
 
 Baseline electrocardiography(ECG) 
 Exercise ECG –Stress test 
 Coronary angiography 
 Exercise radioisotope test (nuclear stress test, myocardial scintigraphy) 
 Magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) 
 Echocardiography(including stress echocardiography) 
 Intravascular ultrasound 
 An x-ray of chest and blood tests can also be performed but the first choice among diagnostic tools is electrocardiogram.
